provenance.instrument: Conshohocken Borough Zoning Ordinance (Chapter 27 Zoning, Ord. 6-2001 of 10-10-2001, as amended), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 CO2517, Borough of Conshohocken (Montgomery County Recorder of Deeds named in 27-825B(3)). District use lists and dimensional standards are text in Parts 10 to 16. The only attachment is the zoning map. New Laws (0)

checks: The code has no accessory dwelling unit. The words searched (accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, granny, caretaker, guest house, servant, living quarters, household employee, conversion, extended family) find only residential conversions (27-825) and the historic conversion rules (27-1906-C)

Uses accessory to dwellings are a garage or carport, parking space, barn, pet shelter, pool, greenhouse, garden shed and home occupations (27-811A). A freestanding accessory building may be at most 350 sq ft and 15 ft tall with a peaked roof, 10 ft with a flat roof (27-811C). Sheds may not be used as residences (27-811D(1))

Residential conversion of an existing single-family detached dwelling into no more than two added units (27-825). The section opens 'The Zoning Hearing Board may grant a special exception', while BR-1, BR-2 and R-O list it as a conditional use before Borough Council (27-1003.7, 27-1103.7, 27-1203.3). Which path applies there is not settled. 27-825C, headed 'Location', says the conversion 'shall be a permitted use in any zoning district'. It says where a conversion may be, not a third path, so a house in any district may be converted by special exception

Conversion standards: each unit at least 400 sq ft plus 100 sq ft a bedroom, a lot of the district single-family minimum plus 2,000 sq ft for each added unit, no more than three units in all, a recorded restriction against further subdivision, no outside change except for safety or design, two ways out for each unit, parking under Part 20 and a shared driveway (27-825). Units at or above the second story need a fire escape (27-825D(4)). On a nonconforming lot or in a nonconforming building, a change from one conforming use to another is a special exception (27-703I)

Historic Residential Conservation Overlay: it covers every lot in a residential district, in addition to the district rules, and wins where they conflict (27-1903-C). A single-family detached dwelling 'constructed more than 50 years ago' may be expanded or altered 'for continued use as a single-family detached dwelling only' (27-1902-C, 27-1904-C). It may be converted only by conditional use from Borough Council, on a showing that it keeps the building, its front and side facades and porches, and mature trees, that the current use is not feasible, that other permitted uses were denied or are not feasible, that the permitted uses give no reasonable rate of return, and that the applicant did not cause the conditions (27-1906-C). The 50 years count back from today, so the cutoff year moves each year

BR-2 permits a two-family detached dwelling (duplex), one unit above the other, by right on 5,000 sq ft, 50 ft wide, with 7 ft side yards (27-1102.4, 27-1105, 27-202). BC permits residential uses above a nonresidential use, not on the street or ground level (27-1302.17). The Fayette Street Corridor Overlay, on parts of R-O and BC along Fayette Street from Elm Street to 12th Avenue, permits the same as an option (27-2302, 27-2303)

No structure may be built, converted or altered for human habitation on an alley lot, a lot with access only on an alley and no public street frontage. 'An existing structure located on an alley lot shall not be converted, altered, or remodeled but may be restored or repaired for an existing use' (27-828)

Parking: 2 spaces per dwelling unit for dwelling types other than multifamily studio and one-bedroom units, which need 1 1/2 (27-2002). A house converted to three units is a multifamily conversion (27-202), so its studio or one-bedroom units may need 1 1/2 each, and Part 20 gives no rule for a fraction. Parking and driveways for residential uses other than a single-family detached dwelling must be paved (27-2005C). No required parking between the front wall of the house and the curb in BR-1, BR-2 and R-O (27-1007, 27-1107, 27-1204.5)

Floodplain Conservation District: 'No new construction, alteration, or improvement of any buildings and any other type of permanent structure, including fences, shall be permitted in the floodway or the one-hundred-year floodplain' and 'New construction of buildings or placement of fill within the one-hundred-year floodplain is prohibited' (27-1714.1A, B). Yet 27-1715 and 27-1716 let an existing structure be improved: no expansion in the floodway that raises the base flood elevation, none in an AE area that raises it more than one foot, none toward the stream bank, and work costing 50% or more of its value must fully comply. The exception in 27-1713.1G reaches only brownfield sites in redevelopment areas

Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board on the hardship findings of 27-611.1. No bar on a use variance. A special exception or variance expires if permits are not obtained within one year (27-613). A lot of record too small to build on may get a variance where more ground is not available (27-802)

Exterior renovations in R-O are reviewed by the Design Review Committee (27-1208). In R-O a conditional use must face Fayette Street, keep the existing building, its front facade and porch, with additions to the rear, keep the front yard landscaped and have no front parking (27-1204). Conditional uses in R-O need a 4,500 sq ft lot, 30 ft wide for a residential use, with 60% impervious cover (80% with shared parking) (27-1206)

Multifamily Dwelling Overlay: multifamily dwellings are a conditional use in BR-1 and BR-2 on a tract of at least two acres, at up to 16 units an acre, with 30 ft yards, 30% building and 70% impervious cover, 35 ft height and units of at least 700 sq ft (27-1802, 27-1803)
A conditional use expires if all permits are not obtained within one year (27-826C). All development must be served by public water and sewer (27-818)
provenance.notes: Zoning office: Conshohocken Borough Zoning Officer. Read in a browser on eCode360 (print view), one page at a time, on 2026-11-16. Read: Parts 6 to 13, Part 15, Part 16, Part 17 (27-1700 to 27-1725), Part 18, Part 19-C, Part 20, Part 22 (SP-4 use list), Part 23 (FCO), 27-202 and code searches. Not read: Parts 1, 3, 4 and 5, Part 14 beyond its use list, 27-1726 to 27-1732, Parts 19 (EDH), 19-A (AQH) and 21, and the end of 27-613. A web search found a group home amendment to 27-823 dated 2024 whose adoption could not be confirmed. The code is current only to 03-06-2024.

term.note: Searched for accessory dwelling, in-law, accessory apartment, garage apartment, second dwelling, ECHO, granny, caretaker, guest house, servant, living quarters, household employee, conversion and extended family, and read the use lists of BR-1, BR-2, R-O, BC, LI, SP-1, SP-2 and SP-3 and 27-811. No ADU use

status.note: No district lists a second dwelling on a single-family lot as an accessory use. An existing house may be converted to up to three units (27-825)

path.note: A second unit on a single-family lot is not a listed use, so the path is a use variance from the Zoning Hearing Board (MPC 910.2). In R-O a use of similar intensity and scale may be a conditional use (see the path for a use not listed). A unit inside an existing house may instead be a residential conversion (see the other paths)

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board, on the findings of 27-611.1. No bar on a use variance

value.name: Residential conversion of an existing house (27-825), house 50 years old or less
value.conditions: An existing single-family detached dwelling into no more than two added units, three units in all. Each unit at least 400 sq ft plus 100 sq ft a bedroom. The lot must hold the district single-family minimum plus 2,000 sq ft for each added unit, and that land is restricted by a recorded deed against further subdivision. No outside change except for safety or improved design, fire escapes to the rear, two ways out for each unit, a fire escape for units at or above the second story, parking under Part 20 with the existing driveway shared. A house on an alley lot may not be converted (27-828). On a nonconforming lot or in a nonconforming building the change of use is also a special exception (27-703I). In R-O a conditional use needs a 4,500 sq ft lot and may cover 60% of it with impervious surfaces (27-1206). A house built more than 50 years ago follows 27-1906-C instead (see that path)

requires.condition: The house was built 50 years ago or less. An older house is a historic single-family detached dwelling
The lot has public street frontage, not only an alley

disputed_path.note: The BR-1, BR-2 and R-O use lists name residential conversions as conditional uses before Borough Council. 27-825C, headed 'Location', says where a conversion may be, not how it is approved

value.note: A house divided into units, not a unit added to it. The lot figures are the single-family minimum plus 2,000 sq ft for one added unit

value.name: Conversion of a historic single-family house (27-1906-C)
value.conditions: A single-family detached dwelling built more than 50 years ago 'may be converted only when approved as a conditional use' by Borough Council. The applicant must show that the building and the look of its front and side facades, porches and windows are kept, mature trees are kept, the current use is not feasible, other uses permitted in the district were denied or are not feasible, adaptive use is not possible, the permitted uses give no reasonable rate of return, and the applicant did not cause the conditions. The 27-825 conversion standards apply as well, since the overlay adds to the district rules (27-1903-C). An existing single-family detached dwelling into no more than two added units, three units in all. Each unit at least 400 sq ft plus 100 sq ft a bedroom. The lot must hold the district single-family minimum plus 2,000 sq ft for each added unit, and that land is restricted by a recorded deed against further subdivision. No outside change except for safety or improved design, fire escapes to the rear, two ways out for each unit, a fire escape for units at or above the second story, parking under Part 20 with the existing driveway shared. A house on an alley lot may not be converted (27-828). On a nonconforming lot or in a nonconforming building the change of use is also a special exception (27-703I)

requires.condition: The house was built more than 50 years ago
The lot has public street frontage, not only an alley

value.note: A hardship showing, not a plain conversion. The 50 years count back from today, so the cutoff year moves each year

value.name: Residential conversion of an existing house in another district (27-825C)
value.conditions: 'Conversion of an existing single-family detached dwelling shall be a permitted use in any zoning district' (27-825C), and the Zoning Hearing Board may grant it as a special exception (27-825). An existing single-family detached dwelling into no more than two added units, three units in all. Each unit at least 400 sq ft plus 100 sq ft a bedroom. The lot must hold the district single-family minimum plus 2,000 sq ft for each added unit, and that land is restricted by a recorded deed against further subdivision. No outside change except for safety or improved design, fire escapes to the rear, two ways out for each unit, a fire escape for units at or above the second story, parking under Part 20 with the existing driveway shared. A house on an alley lot may not be converted (27-828). On a nonconforming lot or in a nonconforming building the change of use is also a special exception (27-703I)

requires.condition: The lot has public street frontage, not only an alley

value.note: For a house that stands in a district that does not list houses. The lot must hold the district single-family minimum plus 2,000 sq ft for each added unit, and these districts set no single-family minimum, so the lot figure is not settled

value.name: Two-family detached dwelling (BR-2)
value.conditions: A two-family building with one dwelling unit above the other (27-202 'Duplex'). Lot 5,000 sq ft and 50 ft wide, front yard 15 ft or the block's building line, rear yard 25 ft, side yards 7 ft, building coverage 40%, impervious cover 60%. Its parking and driveway must be paved (27-2005C)
value.note: A new two-unit building, not a unit added to a house. Turning an existing house into two units is the conversion path. New buildings are barred in the floodplain (27-1714.1B)

value.name: Residential use above a nonresidential use (BC)
value.conditions: 'Residential uses, provided that they are not located on the street or ground levels and are above a nonresidential use'
value.note: Only above a nonresidential use, not over a house

value.name: Residential use above a nonresidential use (Fayette Street Corridor Overlay)
value.conditions: An owner in the overlay may develop under the overlay's rules instead of the district's. 'Residential uses shall not be located on the street or ground level, and shall be above a nonresidential use.' In Zone One (to 4th Avenue) residential uses are multifamily only. Lot minimum 10,000 sq ft in Zone One, 2,000 in Zone Two and 2,500 in Zone Three. Parking 1 space for each efficiency or one-bedroom unit and 1.5 for each larger unit. A house built more than 50 years ago stays under 27-1906-C
value.note: A mixed-use building on Fayette Street from Elm Street to 12th Avenue, not a unit added to a house

value.name: Multifamily dwellings (Multifamily Dwelling Overlay)
value.conditions: Multifamily dwellings by conditional use from Borough Council on a tract of at least two acres, at up to 16 units an acre, with 30 ft front, side and rear yards, 30% building and 70% impervious cover, 35 ft height and units of at least 700 sq ft for one bedroom, 900 for two and 1,100 for three
value.note: An apartment development on a tract, not a unit added to a house

unlisted_use_path.note: R-O lists 'Other uses of similar intensity and scale' as a conditional use before Borough Council. A unit inside the house is closer to a residential conversion, which R-O lists as a conditional use, and a two-family dwelling is listed by right in BR-2. Those may be read as the listed use, not an unlisted one. In R-O a conditional use must keep the existing building and put additions to the rear (27-1204)

unlisted_use_scope.quote: Other uses of similar intensity and scale

historic_bypass.note: The Historic Residential Conservation Overlay limits changes to houses built more than 50 years ago and makes their conversion a conditional use (27-1906-C). It opens no ADU path

districts_read_no_listing.note: BC permits dwellings only above a nonresidential use. LI, SP-1, SP-2, SP-3 and SP-4 permit no dwellings, and SP-3 lists 'Residential use' as not permitted. An existing house in any of them may still be converted (27-825C)

value.condition: 'New construction of buildings or placement of fill within the one-hundred-year floodplain is prohibited.' This reaches a new building on the lot.

'No new construction, alteration, or improvement of any buildings and any other type of permanent structure, including fences, shall be permitted in the floodway or the one-hundred-year floodplain.' Read alone, this reaches work on an existing house too.

disputed_by.note: The floodplain rules 'do not require any changes' to lawfully existing structures, and an improvement to one follows 27-1716: no expansion in the floodway that raises the base flood elevation, none in an AE area that raises it more than one foot, none toward the stream bank, and work costing 50% or more of its value must fully comply

value.condition: A single-family detached dwelling 'constructed more than 50 years ago' may be expanded or altered 'for continued use as a single-family detached dwelling only', and converted only by conditional use on a showing that the current use is not feasible, other uses are not feasible and the permitted uses give no reasonable rate of return.

'No structure shall be erected, constructed, converted, altered, remodeled, restored, or repaired for human habitation on an alley lot.' An alley lot has access only on an alley and no public street frontage. 'An existing structure located on an alley lot shall not be converted, altered, or remodeled but may be restored or repaired for an existing use.' So a house on an alley lot may not be converted to more units.

types_allowed.note: No ADU use. A second unit is only possible through the listed paths

front_yard_barred.note: 'Accessory structures may be erected within the side or rear yard'

setback_side_ft.note: 'not closer than three feet to the rear or side lot line unless the abutting owner or owners provide written consent', with a 4 ft maintenance easement. 5 ft from the edge of an alley cartway

setback_rear_ft.note: Same 3 ft rule. 5 ft from the edge of an alley cartway

accessory_structure_max_sqft.note: 'Any freestanding building used for an accessory use shall not exceed 350 square feet in area'. A garage only for parking may be 450 sq ft

accessory_structure_max_height_ft.note: 15 ft with a peaked roof, 10 ft with a flat roof

spaces_required.note: 'Dwelling unit, all other types: 2 spaces per dwelling unit.' Read for a unit made by conversion. A studio or one-bedroom unit in a multifamily dwelling needs 1 1/2, and a house converted to three units is a multifamily conversion (27-202). Part 20 gives no rule for a fraction of a space

total_on_site.note: Two for each of two dwelling units

setback_front_ft.note: From the ultimate right-of-way, or the building line of most buildings on that side of the block

min_lot_sqft_by_type.note: Single-family semidetached dwelling, per dwelling unit

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached, 40 ft wide. Two-family detached 5,000 sq ft

setback_front_ft.note: From the ultimate right-of-way, or the block's building line, never less than 10 ft from the curb

min_lot_sqft_by_type.note: Single-family semidetached dwelling, per dwelling unit

setback_side_ft_by_type.note: The side not sharing a common wall

min_lot_sqft.note: Single-family detached, 35 ft wide. Conditional uses need 4,500 sq ft (27-1206)

setback_front_ft.note: From the ultimate right-of-way, or the building line of most buildings on the block

min_lot_sqft_by_type.note: Single-family semidetached dwelling, per dwelling unit
